doc.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Taking risks as an artist
summary: She says she never took risks as an artist, and was not born with a career.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: When you talk about Monk and Max talking about making mistakes and when you were talking about "Caged Bird, "I was thinking about taking risks as an artist. Was there a point where you could do that, would do that, and has that -- how has that affected your development, do you think, as an artist?

I never took any risks. Not as an artist. Career-wise, maybe I could say that, but I never took any risks as an artist. I never did that. I didn't go to any other form after I discovered this music and I say okay. I never did that. I'm true to what serves me.
In terms of career or business or anything?
To hell with the career. I wasn't born with a career.
